finding: AUT-079's own blocking question — does MHCflurry 2.1.4 score HLA-C at all — was UNKNOWN from this tree (no mhcflurry installed in the sandbox, by design; CI-only). Settled at rung 0 (WebSearch, ci-escape-hatches §0) rather than dispatching CI blind to find out: MHCflurry's pan-allele Class1PresentationPredictor publishes per-allele motif documentation for individual HLA-C alleles (e.g. the mhcflurry-motifs HLA-C*05:01 page), so HLA-C is scored by the pan-allele models and the item does not collapse. The panel itself (18 common two-field HLA-C alleles) is a good-faith common-allele list, not a cited reference panel — no HLA-C analogue of the A/B panel's '≈IEDB reference breadth' framing was found, and the code comment says so plainly rather than inventing a citation. Because coverage_scan.py calls predictor.predict() ONCE over the whole panel as a batch, an allele MHCflurry cannot score would otherwise raise inside that single call and (under the workflow step's continue-on-error) silently zero out results for every OTHER allele too — not just the unsupported one. Filtered against predictor.supported_alleles before predicting, with the drops named, to avoid that failure mode entirely rather than discover it after a wasted CI run.
